planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring once frost danger has passed, in well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Pink Satin is a California-bred pomegranate selection grown mainly for fresh eating, producing medium-to-large, bright red-skinned fruit filled with soft, pale pink arils that are easy to eat because the seeds inside them are tender rather than hard. The juice is pale, sweet, and notably low in tannic astringency compared to classic dark-red pomegranates, giving it a mild, fruit-punch-like flavor. Trees are vigorous and self-fruitful, can be grown as a large shrub or trained to a small single-trunk tree, and need only modest winter chilling to set fruit reliably. Give plants full sun and well-drained soil, and expect fruit to color up and ripen in early-to-mid fall.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root stock in late winter to spring in well-drained soil in full sun, giving the tree room to grow into a large multi-stemmed shrub or small tree.

directions: Austin is a heritage pomegranate of Middle Eastern origin that has long been passed around home gardens in central Texas, prized for exceptionally heavy, reliable production as well as fruit quality. The large fruit are packed with big, juicy arils that separate from the membrane easily when the fruit is opened, making it a favorite for fresh eating. A single mature tree can produce an outsized crop compared with many other pomegranate varieties, and it performs especially well in regions with long, hot summers. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, and expect fruit to ripen from mid to late in the pomegranate season.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root trees in late winter to spring in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun; established plants tolerate heat and drought well.

directions: Granada is a selection derived from the classic 'Wonderful' pomegranate, producing large, deep red-skinned fruit filled with juicy, dark red arils that are noticeably less tart and more sugary than standard Wonderful fruit. It ripens earlier in the season than Wonderful, which lets gardeners in cooler climates harvest a full crop before fall frosts arrive, and growers in the southern Plains consider it a bit more cold-tolerant in the wood as well. Plants grow as a dense, many-branched shrub or small tree with showy orange-red spring and summer flowers that attract hummingbirds. Note that Granada is a distinct named selection from the similarly spelled heirloom 'Grenada' pomegranate, not an alternate spelling of it.
